narration: You've got multiple debts and you're doing the smart thing — paying off the highest interest rate first. But researchers just found a fatal flaw in that plan.
visual: Dark background. Three credit cards float down from the top, labeled 24.99%, 19.99%, 14.99% APR in red, amber, and blue. Text: 'The smart move?' then amber callout box: 'Researchers found a fatal flaw.'

narration: The debt avalanche says attack 24.99% APR first. On paper, it saves the most interest. But 'on paper' isn't where you actually live.
visual: Light background. Three debt cards stacked vertically by APR — 24.99% card highlighted in red with 'ATTACK FIRST' badge, the other two faded. Green badge pops in: 'Mathematically Optimal'. Dark callout: 'On paper isn't where you live.'

narration: Here's the thing. When that big card barely moves month after month, motivation dies. Most people quit and slide right back into debt.
visual: Dark background. Single red credit card with $4,200 balance and a progress bar that barely creeps forward over 8 animated months. Sad person silhouette slumps below. Red warning box: 'Most people give up.'

narration: Number one — snowball says kill the smallest balance first, whatever the rate. That fast win reloads your motivation for the next one.
visual: Light background. Three cards ordered smallest to largest ($800, $2,400, $4,200). Green 'PAID!' stamp appears on the $800 card. Amber arrow rolls the freed payment into the next card. Box: 'The payment snowballs.'

narration: Harvard researchers tracked real debt payoffs. Snowball users eliminated fourteen percent more debt than avalanche users. Emotional momentum outweighed every dollar of interest math.
visual: Dark background. Animated bar chart — gray Avalanche bar grows to 86%, amber Snowball bar grows taller to 100%. '+14%' amber badge stamps the snowball bar. Callout: 'Snowball users paid off 14% more total debt.'

narration: Find the balance you can kill in ninety days and start today. The best plan isn't perfect math — it's the one you'll actually finish. Follow for more money traps nobody explains.
visual: Light background. Three debt cards flip from red to green one by one, each stamped 'PAID!'. Person silhouette appears with arms raised in celebration. Black CTA box: 'Follow for more money traps nobody explains.'
